pointers.sentence: The documentation's reason: a program working in local time meets errors twice a year, when the clocks change (`docs/topics/i18n/timezones.txt`).

`django.utils.timezone.is_aware` and `is_naive` test exactly that, and a comment says that they, `make_aware` and `make_naive` check nothing about their argument, by design: given `None`, they fail with an `AttributeError` (`django/utils/timezone.py:is_aware`).

`django.utils.timezone.now` is the present: aware in UTC where `USE_TZ` is true, and where it is false a naive reading of the process's clock, which is in `TIME_ZONE` where the settings object could set it ([The settings object](../startup/settings.md)) (`django/utils/timezone.py:now`).

`USE_TZ` is true by default, and pytz has gone, with `make_aware`'s is_dst argument (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`): the documentation points instead to the value's `datetime.datetime.fold` for a local time that happens twice or never (`docs/topics/i18n/timezones.txt`).

`USE_TZ` is true by default, and pytz has gone, with `make_aware`'s is_dst argument (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`): the documentation points instead to the value's `datetime.datetime.fold` for a local time that happens twice or never (`docs/topics/i18n/timezones.txt`).
The **default time zone** is `TIME_ZONE`'s, `"America/Chicago"` unless a project sets it (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

`get_default_timezone` makes a `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` of it on its first call and keeps it, under `functools.lru_cache`; its comment says it is a function so that the setting is not read at import (`django/utils/timezone.py:get_default_timezone`).
`get_current_timezone` gives that value, or the default zone where there is none (`django/utils/timezone.py:get_current_timezone`).

`activate` sets it: a `tzinfo` as it is, a string as a `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`, so that an unknown name fails with `zoneinfo.ZoneInfoNotFoundError`, and anything else is refused with `ValueError`, `"Invalid timezone: 5"` for a 5 (`django/utils/timezone.py:activate`).

`override`, a context manager and a decorator, remembers on entry the value present and activates its zone, or deactivates for `None`; on exit it puts the remembered value back, or deactivates where there was none (`django/utils/timezone.py:override`).

`get_current_timezone_name` and `get_default_timezone_name` name a zone through `_get_timezone_name`: by the name it gives without a date, as a fixed offset does, and otherwise as a string, which for a `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` is its key, `"Europe/Amsterdam"` (`django/utils/timezone.py:_get_timezone_name`).

The name is what a `Trunc` or an `Extract` gives the backend for its SQL ([Transforms and database functions: `Transform` and `Func`](../sql/functions.md)) (`django/db/models/functions/datetime.py:TimezoneMixin.get_tzname`).
The documentation's reason: a request carries nothing to choose one by, as Accept-Language does a language (`docs/topics/i18n/timezones.txt`).
`django.utils.timezone.localtime` converts an aware datetime into the current zone, or one it is given, and with no value converts the present (`django/utils/timezone.py:localtime`).
`make_naive` converts the same way and drops the zone (`django/utils/timezone.py:make_naive`).

A template converts each aware datetime it writes, through `template_localtime`, unless `USE_TZ` or the template's own flag says not to or a filter has converted it already (`django/utils/timezone.py:template_localtime`); the tags are in [The libraries to load: static, i18n, l10n, tz and cache](../templates/loadable-libraries.md).

`django.utils.timezone.make_aware` takes a naive datetime as a reading of the current zone's clock, or another zone's, and attaches the zone with `datetime.datetime.replace`, refusing an aware value with `ValueError`; a comment warns that this "may be wrong around DST changes" (`django/utils/timezone.py:make_aware`).
`_datetime_ambiguous_or_imaginary` finds such readings: the zone gives the value one offset as it is and another with its fold flipped (`django/utils/timezone.py:_datetime_ambiguous_or_imaginary`).

`from_current_timezone`, through which a form's datetime field passes what it read, refuses such a reading with a `ValidationError` of code `"ambiguous_timezone"` ([The built-in form fields](../forms/field-types.md#dates-and-times)) (`django/forms/utils.py:from_current_timezone`).

`TimeFormat` gives such a value no zone, so the format letters `"e"`, `"O"`, `"T"`, `"Z"` and `"I"` write nothing ([Writing numbers, dates and durations](writing-values.md)) (`django/utils/dateformat.py:TimeFormat.__init__`).

A model's datetime field given a naive value warns and makes it aware in the default zone, not the current one; its comment expects an exception at a change of the clocks, and under `zoneinfo` none comes, so a naive 02:30 on 29 March becomes 01:30 UTC ([The field classes](../models/field-types.md)) (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:DateTimeField.get_prep_value`).

The date views make each boundary of a period midnight in the current zone, for a datetime field ([The date views](../views/dates.md)) (`django/views/generic/dates.py:DateMixin._make_date_lookup_arg`).
